s3_put_usd_per_1000_requests.note: Not confirmed against the us-west-2 catalog. Needs a regional primary receipt before any spend decision.

s3_get_usd_per_1000_requests.note: Not confirmed against the us-west-2 catalog. No routine GET is modeled.

kms_key_usd_per_month.source: AWS awskms us-west-2 price list version 20260911124601, published 2026-09-11T12:46:01Z
kms_key_usd_per_month.note: One customer managed key version. The template sets EnableKeyRotation, and AWS adds 1 USD per month for each of the first two rotations (prorated hourly), capped after the second (https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/), so storage can rise from 1 to 3 USD per month. 1 USD is the figure before any rotation.

kms_rotation_billed_versions_max.source: https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/ ('the first and second rotation of the key adds $1/month (prorated hourly) ... capped at the second rotation'), page saved by the coordinator
kms_rotation_billed_versions_max.note: Number of rotations that add a key-version charge. A count from AWS's pricing page text, not a catalog rate, so it is not regionally verified.

kms_usd_per_10000_requests.source: AWS awskms us-west-2 price list version 20260911124601, published 2026-09-11T12:46:01Z
kms_usd_per_10000_requests.note: The catalog prices one request at 0.000003 USD.

kms_free_requests_per_month.source: AWS awskms us-west-2 price list version 20260911124601, published 2026-09-11T12:46:01Z
kms_free_requests_per_month.note: A global free tier shared across every AWS KMS use in the account and all regions. The model cannot assume the whole allowance is unused; the peak exposure uses none of it.

secrets_manager_usd_per_secret_month.source: AWS AWSSecretsManager us-west-2 price list version 20260911124610, published 2026-09-11T12:46:10Z

data_transfer_out_usd_per_gb.note: Not confirmed against the us-west-2 catalog.

credit_mode.template: deploy/hosted/stack.json sets no CreditSpecification, so the instance takes the account default for T4g
credit_mode.requirement: An owner confirms unlimited or standard mode. Unlimited bills the surplus above. Standard bills none and throttles the node at baseline, a capacity limit instead of a cost. The model sets neither and changes no infrastructure, threshold or retention.

unknown_rates.embeddings_usd_per_1k_tokens: pending task42 provider/serving-provider pin (perplexity/pplx-embed-v1-0.6b terms are unqualified per docs/launch/hosted-plan.md)
unknown_rates.cloudwatch_logs_volume_gb_per_month: rate is priced (cloudwatch_logs_ingest_usd_per_gb) but no log shipping is wired yet (ops go through SSM Run Command per ADR 014); volume unknown pending T23.53 telemetry
unknown_rates.cloudwatch_custom_metrics_count: rate is priced (cloudwatch_custom_metric_usd_per_month) but T23.53's metric cardinality is not yet implemented
unknown_rates.s3_get_list_restore: no routine GET/List/restore is modeled (no scheduled integrity check or restore drill in the current design); a restore drill or T23.50 recovery testing adds GET/List cost on top of this baseline, not included here
unknown_rates.control_db_lifetime_growth: control.db is copied whole into every snapshot and no runtime code prunes committed reservations or audit_log rows, so it grows with lifetime writes and recalls. The 20 MB constant is a scenario assumption at snapshot time, not a lifetime bound. Each scenario reports a sensitivity at sampled row sizes, which is not an upper bound
unknown_rates.ec2_cpu_credit_mode: the template sets no CreditSpecification, so a t4g.small uses the account default for T4g, which is unverified (AWS's default is unlimited). Unlimited mode bills surplus credits; standard mode bills none and throttles at baseline. An owner must confirm the mode; the model sets neither
unknown_rates.s3_multipart_requests: aws s3 cp uploads objects larger than the CLI multipart threshold in parts, and each part is a request. The deployed CLI's setting is not in the template; each scenario reports a sensitivity at the CLI default, not in any subtotal
unknown_rates.global_free_allowances: the KMS request allowance and the data-transfer allowance are account-wide, and the shared AWS account's other use is unknown, so neither can be assumed unused; the peak exposure uses none of them
unknown_rates.email_peak_volume: Resend cost is modeled from average logins per month, and an average day is not a maximum: a burst past the 100-per-day free cap needs a paid tier. Peak login volume is unknown, so no email maximum is claimed

measurements.note: A record changes only the scenario and quantity it names. A scenario with no record is priced on assumptions, and a measurement is never evidence of capacity acceptance.

idle_0_accounts.assumption: no signups yet; fixed infrastructure cost floor

ec2_burst_credits.note: mean-case assumption, not a peak, and only if the account default credit mode is unlimited; see peak_exposure

kms_key.note: key storage before any rotation; the template enables rotation, so it can reach 3 USD/month; see peak_exposure

secrets_manager_api_calls.note: assumes 5 restarts/month reading all 4 secrets at boot (ADR 014); no other Secrets Manager traffic modeled

s3_storage_backups.note: backup.sh writes a unique timestamped prefix every run (never overwritten); Expiration(30d)+NoncurrentVersionExpiration(30d) in series gives each object a ~60-day bucket lifetime, so ~1441 hourly backup-sets are retained at steady state, the deployed-template baseline -- see docs/launch/hosted-economics.md. The control database is a scenario assumption at snapshot time, not a lifetime bound; see unknown_categories.control_db_lifetime_growth.

kms_requests.note: SSE-KMS attaches ~1 KMS request per S3 backup PUT (assumed; no bucket key is set in the template); 20000/month global free tier applied before this line, and an account-wide allowance cannot be assumed unused, so peak_exposure uses none of it.

data_transfer_out.note: 4096B/recall response, 1024B/write request assumed; first 100 GB/month free applied before this line, and an account-wide allowance cannot be assumed unused, so peak_exposure uses none of it.

email.note: assumes 10 magic-link emails/account/month, an average day and not a maximum; Resend free tier is 3000/month capped 100/day

peak_exposure.note: Replaces the mean-case CPU surplus, the pre-rotation KMS key, and the free-allowance offsets on KMS requests and transfer with their worst case. Every unknown category stays out, so this is not a full maximum. It is not a spending recommendation.

per_plan_contribution.note: Fixed shared-node infrastructure (EC2, EBS, EIP, KMS key, Secrets Manager storage, CloudWatch alarms) is not allocated per-plan -- one node serves every tenant. Only usage-driven categories are apportioned, by each plan's share of total customer storage bytes.

rebuild_reembed_tokens.note: assumes 30 cold reopens/account/month and 1% of stored facts missing a vector per reopen; index.RecoverMemorySearch (ADR 014) only re-embeds facts actually missing a vector, so this is a conservative upper-bound guess, not a measurement

readiness_tokens.note: assumes a /readyz probe every 5 minutes (matches the CloudWatch alarm 300s evaluation period) with a fixed ~10-token bounded embedding call per ADR 014

The 20 MB constant is a scenario assumption at snapshot time, not a lifetime bound. Each scenario reports a sensitivity at sampled row sizes, which is not an upper bound

s3_multipart_requests.basis: ceil(snapshot bytes / chunk) parts per backup, less one request per object already counted; KMS requests per part are unverified and not counted; not in any subtotal
s3_multipart_requests.reason: aws s3 cp uploads objects larger than the CLI multipart threshold in parts, and each part is a request. The deployed CLI's setting is not in the template; each scenario reports a sensitivity at the CLI default, not in any subtotal

ec2_cpu_credit_mode.reason: the template sets no CreditSpecification, so a t4g.small uses the account default for T4g, which is unverified (AWS's default is unlimited). Unlimited mode bills surplus credits; standard mode bills none and throttles at baseline. An owner must confirm the mode; the model sets neither

global_free_allowances.reason: the KMS request allowance and the data-transfer allowance are account-wide, and the shared AWS account's other use is unknown, so neither can be assumed unused; the peak exposure uses none of them

email_peak_volume.reason: Resend cost is modeled from average logins per month, and an average day is not a maximum: a burst past the 100-per-day free cap needs a paid tier. Peak login volume is unknown, so no email maximum is claimed

ceiling_note: The historical USD 60/month figure is a ceiling, not a budget target or new spend authorization (docs/launch/hosted-plan.md).
citation_note: Rates marked aws_regional_catalog_primary are read from AWS's own US West (Oregon) price lists, with a receipt file, rate code, source hash and publication date each (docs/launch/evidence/T23.60/aws-rates/, s3-rate.json). Rates marked secondary_summary_not_regionally_verified (S3 request prices, data transfer) and vendor_page_secondary (Resend) still need a regional primary or vendor receipt. Receipts imply no account, credit, free-tier or spend authority. The retention baseline is the deployed template's; any thinning proposal is unapproved and not modeled.
